establishing that 12Partition is NP-hard.

fields.explanation: The original equal-copy construction omits every K*4^(6-i) positional term and repeats input values despite the source set convention; it is not an instance of the recorded reduction. The replacement keeps the exact Lemma3 assertion and its entire construction. T={9,10,11,12,13,15},m=2,B=35,K=71 has sum70 and35/4<t<35/2. For each0-basedi andj=1..4 use t_i+j*71*4^(6-i). The24 values are distinct and positive. BlockA takesj=1,4 for each index, blockB takesj=2,3. Both have12 elements and sum1,938,440, yet each contains exactly two copies of each of six indices, refuting Lemma3. This replacement does not assert that T is a NO3Partition instance. The selected theorem certifies the source-qualified primary counterexample. Historical auxiliary sweeps are not silently promoted to universal statements.
fields.flaw: Lemma 3 asserts that every equal-sum 12-element block in a valid partition of the source positional construction consists of all four shifted copies at exactly three indices. The source-exact replacement gives two equal-sum 12-element blocks, each taking two shifted copies at each of six indices. This refutes that lemma; it does not establish that a NO 3-Partition instance maps to a YES 12-Partition instance.

fields.witness: T = {9,10,11,12,13,15}, m=2, B=35, K=1+sum(T)=71. For zero-based i=0,...,5 and j=1,...,4 define s_i^(j)=t_i+j*71*4^(6-i), exactly the source formula in one-based indexing. A contains j=1,4 at every index; B contains j=2,3 at every index. The24 transformed positive integers are pairwise distinct, A and B are disjoint12-element blocks partitioning them, and each block sums to1,938,440. Both blocks contain two copies at each of six indices, rather than four copies at three indices. Thus the source Lemma3 is false.
